item.title: [World news | The Guardian] Weather tracker: Typhoon Saudel causes mass evacuations in south-east China
item.description:
Torrential rain causes widespread damage; while north-west South Africa hit by thunderstorms and central-southern US faces oppressive heat

Typhoon Saudel brought days of torrential rain to Zhejiang, Jiangxi, Fujian and Guangdong provinces in south-east China last week. The city of Putian, in Fujian province, recorded 416.5mm of rain in a 24-hour period between Thursday and Friday, with surrounding villages recording more than 500mm in the same period. In Fujian, authorities estimate that almost 600,000 people were evacuated from high-risk, flood-prone areas. A further 128,000 people in 53 counties were also affected across Jiangxi, with emergency evacuations affecting 9,000 people.

Flooding, landslips and infrastructure damage were reported widely in the region. More than 2,500 teachers and students were trapped in a school compound in the Zhejiang city of Wenzhou on Wednesday after extreme rainfall caused flash floods in low-lying areas. At least 1,260 people reportedly had to be rescued in Putian after a river embankment collapsed on Thursday, flattening 100 homes. On Saturday, a landslip in a village of Suichuan county, in Jiangxi province, killed three people and nine others remaining missing.

The fundamentals of our economy [were] hollowed out through a series of past policy decisions, political power was centralised, weakening the relationships between the people, the businesses and the institutions who can make things happen beyond Whitehall. The economic enablers were privatised and outsourced, leaving accountability to a thicket of arm’s length bodies and regulators, too often without the predictability or the pace that underpins a thriving market economy. And our country was deindustrialised as the cost to make anything, to build anything here soared, and our dependence on unreliable sources grew, including in areas critical to our national security and sovereignty.

Let me be clear, I recognise that the costs of business, its energy bills, regulation, burdens, planning constraints, labour costs, have grown since Covid and I want to draw the line.

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] Israeli ministers call for sanctions on Britain over Falkland Islands
item.description:
Israeli ministers call for sanctions on Britain over Falkland Islands

Submitted by Imran Mulla on Mon, 09/07/2026 - 23:05
The remarks are understood to be a response to the British government's plan to sanction Israeli settlements
Britain's Prime Minister Andy Burnham inside 10 Downing Street in central London on September 3, 2026. (AFP)
Off

Israeli Ministers Itamar Ben Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich have called for Israel to sanction Britain over the Falkland Islands, as the UK government prepares to announce a ban on trade with illegal Israeli settlements in occupied Palestinian territory.

Smotrich, Israel's finance minister, called for the expulsion of the British ambassador to Israel and said: "We will not be a trampled doormat of an antisemitic government, in a country conquered by radical Islam, trying to save itself from economic and social decline by attacking Jews and the State of Israel. The British Mandate in the Land of Israel is over." 

Ben Gvir, the security minister, posted on X in Spanish calling on Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to sanction Britain for its "occupation" of the Falkland Islands.

Ben Gvir wrote: "It's time for the state of Israel to publicly recognize that the Malvinas Islands [the Argentine name for the Falkland Islands] are Argentine territory under occupation, which the British violently steal from the Argentine people.

"The British are not content with merely occupying the territory; they also carry out oil drilling there and steal the money from the Argentine people."

Ben Gvir added: "I call upon Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to recognise Argentina's sovereignty over the Malvinas Islands and to impose sanctions on Great Britain as long as the occupation continues."

MEE has asked the British Foreign Office for comment.

Argentina and the UK both assert sovereignty over the South Atlantic archipelago, but the vast majority of the territory's 3,600 residents back British rule.

Last week Argentinian President Javier Milei declared that Argentina's national sovereignty had been "violated" and that his country would defend its interests "tooth and nail, no matter who it bothers".

Milei threatened sanctions on oil firms that seek to drill around the Falkland Islands, adding that the "winds of change" favoured Argentina's claim to them.

US President Donald Trump suggested last week he would not back Britain if Argentina was to invade the Falkland Islands.

The comments by Ben Gvir and Smotrich are understood to come in response to Britain's plans to unveil a raft of policies targeting Israeli settlements on Tuesday, including a trade ban.

Last week the Israeli government threatened Britain with retaliation, with Foreign Minister Gideon Saar warning: "If Britain acts against Israel, Israel will act against Britain."

British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has not spoken to his Israeli counterpart since he became prime minister in July.

He reportedly briefed Trump on his plans to introduce sanctions on Istael on Monday afternoon. The Trump administration is understood to strongly oppose the British government's approach.

Tensions between Britain and Israel are likely to escalate.

The movement said Israel attempted to "obliterate evidence" through "removing, crushing and relocating the rubble", despite the presence of "bodies of thousands of missing people and material evidence of the crimes of genocide committed by the occupation over two years".

"Tampering with these sites, with what they contain of bodies and evidences, constitutes a violation of international law and the International Court of Justice's ruling calling for the preservation of evidence, as well as an affront to the dignity of the martyrs and the right of their families to recover and bury the bodies of their loved ones," the statement read. 

Hamas urged the UN, international courts and relevant authorities to "take urgent action to protect these sites" as well as deploying international investigation teams and forensic experts to oversee the recovery of bodies and the documentation and preservation of evidence. 

"We emphasize that the swift removal of rubble and the reconstruction of Gaza are an urgent humanitarian and national necessity and an inalienable right of our people," it added.

item.title: [World news | The Guardian] Why India’s economic data has sparked a furore
item.description:
India’s statistical system once commanded respect, and its data on economic and social indicators was considered rigorous – that appears to have eroded

There isn’t much that we Indians agree on these days. GDP numbers are no exception. Last week, India released glowing GDP numbers for the latest quarter – 7.8% growth – higher than the forecast 7%. It sparked a furore.

Subhash Garg, a former finance secretary under Narendra Modi’s government and now a critic, reframed what Modi called a “herculean feat” as mere smoke and mirrors. According to Garg, the government revised last year’s current-price GDP downwards to inflate this year’s number – he believes the real growth is only 2.6%.

item.description:
Fighting in Yemen kills, wounds nearly 900, as thousands left displaced

Nearly 900 people have been wounded or killed as a result of renewed fighting that began last week, the World Health Organisation (WHO) reported.

WHO indicated that 670 of those casualties are coming from Taiz and the west coast front.

Moreover, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) recorded the displacement of roughly 18,500 people since hostilities began.

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] Watch: Russia calls for Iran to be included in the Mecca Agreement
item.description:
Watch: Russia calls for Iran to be included in the Mecca Agreement

Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov has called for Iran to be included in the Mecca Agreement, a trilateral mutual defence pact signed by Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan last month. 

Speaking at a meeting with students and faculty at the Moscow State Institute of International Relations (MGIMO), Lavrov said Iran’s participation in a Gulf security system would be an important move toward ensuring regional stability and would be a 'practical step' towards Moscow's vision for the region.

One Nation policy will leave people $25k worse off at retirement, Mulino says

Superannuation is kicking off again today with One Nation pushing to allow people to divert 3% of their superannuation to their rent or mortgage.

It took us decades to get to 12% superannuation guarantee and that’s a level that will provide people with a high level of dignity and security in retirement.

To do what the One Nation party is suggesting will see somebody who is 30 years old, $25,000 worse off at retirement and a couple around $50,000 worse off.

I’m deeply sceptical of giving any government, whether I was in charge, or Anika Wells is in charge, I’m deeply sceptical of giving any government the power to decide what you read on your phone.
